evidence: Allocation record count is exactly 24, 4, 2 and 1 for saveat 1h, 6h, 12h and 24h respectively.
Allocation record times lie on the saveat grid in every tested case.
Shorter saveat exposes retained Basin storage to management reoptimization earlier within the same one-day horizon.
Total physical UserDemand supply rises monotonically as saveat decreases: approximately 16.0192, 20.0207, 24.5179 and 29.0918 m3 for 24h, 12h, 6h and 1h clocks.
Retained Basin storage falls correspondingly while the 32 m3 physical ledger closes.
For a fixed saveat, priority order changes recipient allocation/delivery but not total physical supply or Basin endpoint within tolerance.
interpretation: In the pinned real Ribasim allocation configuration, solver.saveat is not an observationally neutral output setting. It participates in allocation timing. More frequent save boundaries cause state-dependent management reoptimization of physically retained Basin water within the nominal allocation.dt=86400 s interval.
upstream_context: Deltares/Ribasim PR #3218 explicitly notes that a coupler can rely on allocation calls at multiples of saveat and characterizes that synchronization as brittle/not what saveat was meant for; the same loop structure was observed on current upstream main.

duplicate_attempt.reason: A later trigger commit inherited preregistered DUMMY-19I files, which the frozen DUMMY-19G runner correctly rejected as unexpected branch delta.

boundaries: Do not call the upstream behavior a defect; upstream itself frames it as a brittle synchronization/design concern.
DUMMY-19G quantifies the tested pinned implementation only.
DUMMY-19H is required to isolate repeated management reoptimization from purely physical/output numerical effects.
No SWAP/MODFLOW substitution or production prescription.
